the tensile strength of earlywood is 3 times greater than the strength of latewood, the modulus of elasticity is 2 times greater, and the strain to failure is 3.5 times greater.
the tensile strength of latewood was higher than the tensile strength calculated for the mixture of latewood and earlywood.

the effect of moisture content on the mechanical properties along the grains of Scots pine earlywood and late wood.
the effect of MC on mechanical properties of early- and latewood of pine wood, which are important for wood utilization.
the effect of MC and wood structure (earlywood and latewood), and the effect of the combination of these factors on tensile mechanical properties of Scots pine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the tensile properties along the grains in Scots pine wood of low and high MC are determined by the tensile properties of earlywood, but the effect of MC on latewood is more significant than on earlywood.

, for the Scots pine wood studied, the tensile mechanical parameters of earlywood and that of latewood are different and depend on the MC, but the mechanical parameters calculated from the rule mixtures for both earlywood and that for latewood are similar to those found for samples containing both zones.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the tensile stress test the effect of MC was similar in both earlywood and in latewood of Scots Pine.
the tensile properties of wood along the grains depend not only on MC, but also on the type of wood (earlywood or latewood).
the mechanical properties of Scots pine wood along the grains were not significantly influenced by the moisture content of the wood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanical properties of the wood of Scots pine are determined not only by the MC but also by the type and the proportion of wood tissues.
the tensile properties of Scots pine wood are determined by the mechanical properties of the individual zones (earlywood and latewood), and not by the properties of the wood as a mixture of the two.
the rule of mixures can be used in calculating the mechanical properties of wood with earlywood and latewoood, even when their MCs differ.
